brief: A three-storey cabinet with at least three drawers.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: piece:0,0,0;full (level 0) + piece:0,0,1;full (level 1) + piece:0,0,2;full (level 2) with snaps snap:0,0,0;full and snap:0,0,1;full form a vertical three-storey column (0,0,0 through 0,0,2).

drawer:0#1,0#cut (level 0 e:slide), drawer:1#1,0#cut (level 1 e:slide), drawer:2#1,0#cut (level 2 e:slide) on half-w bases piece:1,0,0/1/2;half-w give three slide drawers, one per storey. Additionally notch:0#0,1#notch1, notch:1#0,1#notch1, notch:2#0,1#notch1 are hex-drawer-frame-notch-fm frames (notch drawer frames) providing three more drawer positions at 0,1 on each level; total 6 drawer positions.

finish.summary: Built three-storey column at 0,0,0-2 with three slide drawers on the east half-bases (one per level) plus three notch-drawer frames on the south side. check_build reports meshClash clear but UNSUPPORTED errors on piece:1,0,1;half-w and piece:1,0,2;half-w (upper half-bases flagged not held up) and 12 OPEN_CAP_FACE info warnings; no new capping/joint-locking applied per your request to start nothing new.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
